quick: 1000-1250 mg/m2 IV over 30 min, schedule by tumor
CBC before each dose, LFTs, renal function
summary: Gemcitabine is an intravenous nucleoside antimetabolite used for pancreatic, lung, breast and ovarian cancers. Dosed by body surface area (1000-1250 mg/m2) over 30 minutes on tumor-specific schedules. Myelosuppression is dose-limiting; infusion >60 minutes or more-than-weekly dosing increases toxicity.
indications: Advanced ovarian cancer relapsing >=6 months after platinum therapy (with carboplatin)
First-line metastatic breast cancer after anthracycline failure (with paclitaxel)
Pancreatic cancer (single agent), including locally advanced or metastatic

dosage.d: 1000 mg/m2 IV over 30 min weekly x7 then 1 week rest; then weekly x3 of each 28-day cycle
1000 mg/m2 Days 1,8,15 of 28-day cycle OR 1250 mg/m2 Days 1,8 of 21-day cycle
1250 mg/m2 IV over 30 min Days 1 and 8 of 21-day cycle
1000 mg/m2 IV over 30 min Days 1 and 8 of 21-day cycle

admin: For intravenous use only; infuse over 30 minutes
Do NOT prolong infusion beyond 60 minutes or dose more often than once weekly - increases toxicity
Reconstitute and dilute per protocol; use cytotoxic handling precautions
Check absolute neutrophil and platelet counts before each dose and reduce/withhold for myelosuppression
Assess hepatic and renal function before and periodically during treatment
moa: A pyrimidine nucleoside analog (2',2'-difluorodeoxycytidine). After intracellular phosphorylation to active diphosphate and triphosphate forms, it inhibits ribonucleotide reductase and is incorporated into DNA, causing chain termination ('masked chain termination') and inhibition of DNA synthesis, leading to apoptosis. Activity is cell-cycle (S-phase) specific.
preg: Can cause fetal harm based on mechanism and animal data; contraindicated in pregnancy. Advise effective contraception for patients and male partners during and after treatment.
lact: Discontinue breastfeeding during treatment and for a period after the last dose due to potential for serious adverse effects in the infant.
renal: Use with caution; gemcitabine has been associated with hemolytic uremic syndrome and renal failure. Monitor renal function; withhold for clinically significant impairment.
hepatic: Use with caution; fatal and severe hepatotoxicity reported. Monitor liver tests; reduce or withhold for significant impairment or rising bilirubin/transaminases.

major: Concurrent thoracic radiotherapy - severe radiosensitization, mucositis and pneumonitis
Live vaccines - risk of disseminated infection in immunosuppressed patients
moderate: Other myelosuppressive agents - additive marrow toxicity
interactions.diagnostics: Causes neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, anemia, and may elevate liver enzymes and bilirubin.

serious: Severe myelosuppression with infection or bleeding

monitoring: Complete blood count with platelets before each dose
Liver function tests at baseline and periodically
Renal function and urinalysis (proteinuria, hematuria) for HUS
Signs of capillary leak or neurologic changes (PRES)
counsel: Report fever, chills or signs of infection immediately (low blood counts)
Report unusual bruising, bleeding, or shortness of breath/cough
Use effective contraception during and after treatment
Flu-like symptoms after dosing are common; report if severe
pk: Short (~42-94 min); depends on infusion duration
Store vials at 20-25 C; reconstituted solution per label, do not refrigerate (crystallization)
pearls: Myelosuppression is dose-limiting - check ANC and platelets before every dose.
Keep infusion at 30 minutes and no more than weekly; longer/more frequent dosing raises toxicity.
Watch for hemolytic uremic syndrome - monitor renal function and urinalysis.
Potent radiosensitizer - avoid concurrent thoracic radiation.
missed: Doses are administered on a fixed cycle schedule by the oncology team; a missed or delayed dose is rescheduled by the clinician based on blood counts and tolerance, not self-administered.
overdose: No specific antidote. Anticipated toxicities are myelosuppression, paresthesias and severe rash. Provide supportive care with blood count monitoring, growth factors/transfusions, and management of infection or bleeding as needed.
